title: Path to Impact: New Hire 120-Day Ops & Benefit Orientation
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook provides a practical, step-by-step 120-day onboarding and benefits orientation for new hires at Redwood Inference. It balances immediate operational access, early contribution goals, and benefit enrollment milestones so that new teammates reach sustained impact quickly and with clarity. This page is intended for new hires, hiring managers, people-ops, and assigned buddies.

Who should use this

- New hires entering any technical or cross-functional role.
- Hiring managers coordinating a new hire’s ramp.
- People-ops and IT teams provisioning access and benefits.
- Assigned buddies and mentors who will guide day-to-day integration.

Quick start checklist (first 48 hours)

1) Complete HR welcome form and benefits pre-enrollment.
2) Verify Okta SSO account and set MFA (Authenticator + recovery email).
3) Join core Slack channels: #all, #team-announce, #engineering-ops (or product equivalent).
4) Claim GitHub account and accept org invitation (organization: redwood-inference).
5) Access Confluence and complete the "New Hire Acknowledgements" page.
6) Meet your manager and buddy for a 30-minute kickoff meeting.

First-Week Objectives (days 1–7)

- Administrative: Confirm payroll, health plan enrollment window, and expense policy understanding. Benefits enrollment deadline is 30 days from start date; action required via the People Ops portal.
- Operational: Confirm access to developer tools (GitHub, CI/CD pipeline, internal artifact store), communication tools (Slack, Email), and ticketing (Jira).
- Social: 2 x 1:1 scheduled with cross-functional partners (security, infra, product) and a team intro meeting.
- Learning: Complete the "Security & Data Handling for New Hires" micro-course (approx 90 minutes).

Typical 120-day plan (high-level goals)

Week 1: Setup and context
- Gain required access and complete required trainings.
- Deliver a short "Intro & Goals" doc in Confluence for your manager and buddy.

Weeks 2–4: Small, meaningful contributions
- Own a small ticket/bug or documentation improvement that touches production code or customer docs.
- Demonstrate end-to-end flow: from issue to code to CI to deployment preview.

Months 2–3 (days 31–90): Expand scope
- Drive a cross-team micro-project (e.g., infra monitoring rule, a reproducible integration test, or a product small feature).
- Complete role-specific competency checkpoints (see Role Ladder Summary below).

Months 3–4 (days 91–120): Sustainable ownership
- Transition at least one operational task or area to stable ownership.
- Present a 15-minute "What I shipped" demo in the team retro and capture learnings in Confluence.

Role Ladder Summary (concise guidance)

- IC-1 (Associate): Focus on learning systems, shipping small changes, and addressing code review feedback.
- IC-2 (Engineer): Own feature slices, mentor interns/juniors, and begin owning SLIs for a service.
- IC-3 (Senior): Drive architecture choices, own large cross-cutting projects, and coach peers.
- Staff+ (Principal/Staff): Define roadmaps, represent the company externally, and lead multi-team programs.

Each role ladder includes competency milestones for technical deliverables, cross-team collaboration, impact metrics, and mentoring responsibilities. For detailed competency rubrics, see the related role pages in the Roles & Career space.

Benefits orientation (what to prioritize and how to enroll)

- Health & Dental: Enrollment window is 30 days from start date. Action steps: Log into People Ops portal -> Benefits -> Enroll. Keep receipts for any opt-out paperwork.
- 401(k): Enrollment available immediately; employer match vests over 12 months.
- Wellness stipend: Claim via expense portal (limit $200 / quarter).
- Parental leave & sabbatical: Review policy in Benefits space and discuss eligibility with People Ops for planning.

People Ops contact for benefits: benefits@redwood.com (response SLA: 2 business days).

Access Matrix (who to contact to get things done)

| Resource | Owner / Team | How to request | Expected SLA |
|---------|-------------|---------------|-------------|
| Okta / SSO | IT / People Ops | Auto-provision via offer letter; re-requests: it-requests@redwood.com | 4 business hours |
| GitHub org | Engineering Tools | Manager approves invite; toolchain@redwood.com for escalations | 1 business day |
| Jira project access | Eng Ops | Manager grant + jira-requests@redwood.com | 1 business day |
| Cloud dev environment | Infra | Infra runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking | 2 business days |
| Payroll and tax forms | Finance | Upload to People Ops portal -> Payroll | 3 business days |

Manager responsibilities (must do list)

- Provide a role-specific 120-day success plan within 48 hours of start.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 12 weeks, then switch cadence to biweekly unless mutually agreed.
- Assign a peer buddy and confirm at least two cross-team intros in week 1.
- Ensure the new hire has at least one scoped, ownerable task by the end of week 2.
- Run a 60-day feedback checkpoint and a 120-day review (documented in Confluence).

Buddy responsibilities (day-to-day support)

- Be the go-to person for quick questions about team conventions and tooling.
- Review the new hire’s first small PR and provide actionable feedback.
- Arrange a "Lunch & Learn" or pairing session in the first 30 days.

Hiring handoff checklist (recruiter -> manager -> people-ops)

1) Recruiter: Final offer package confirmed, candidate accepts, send offer metadata to People Ops (title, manager, start date, salary band).
2) Manager: Confirm onboarding buddy and initial 120-day goals.
3) People Ops: Kick off provisioning workflows, benefits pre-enroll email, and welcome calendar invites.
4) IT/Infra: Ensure required service quotas and sandbox access are available by day 1.

Example commands and templates

- Requesting an additional GitHub team: create a Jira ticket using the "Access Request" template with fields: username, team-name, justification.

- Quick CLI snippet to verify Okta session (for engineers):

  $ okta whoami
  email: asha.patel@redwood.com
  status: active

- Template: 120-day goal doc (copy into your team Confluence space)
  - Problem statement
  - Success metrics (quantitative if possible)
  - Key stakeholders and collaborators
  - Timeline and milestones

Operational excellence expectations

- New hires in engineering are expected to understand the team's SLIs within 60 days and to be able to run the standard profiling and local reproduction steps without assistance by day 90.
- Security & compliance trainings must be completed within 14 days of start; completion is required for continued access to production systems.

Escalations and critical contacts

- People Ops (benefits / payroll): benefits@redwood.com (SLA 2 business days)
- IT / Access escalations: it-requests@redwood.com (SLA 4 business hours)
- Security incident triage: security-oncall@redwood.com (pager: see Security oncall rota)

Frequently asked questions (short answers)

Q: How long until I can push to main?
A: No direct pushes to protected branches. New hires should open PRs and request at least one reviewer. Privileged write permissions are granted based on demonstrated review quality and tenure, typically after 90 days.

Q: Who signs me up for health/dental?
A: You enroll yourself via the People Ops portal; People Ops can assist if you miss the 30-day window.

Q: What should I prioritize in week 1?
A: Confirm access, meet your manager and buddy, and ship a small documentation or configuration change to learn the end-to-end flow.
